# Case Study

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Case Study: Home Prices in King County, WA

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE,warning = FALSE,message = FALSE,fig.align = 'center')
library(tidyverse)
library(moderndive)
library(gridExtra)
houses <- read_csv("data/house.csv")
# houses <- houses %>% select(price,sqft_living,sqft_above,bedrooms)
```

**What's the relationship between a home's square footage and number of bedrooms on the home's sale price?**

```{r}
glimpse(houses)
```
<br>

We'll focus on **four variables**: Sale price (*response*); and square footage, above-ground square footage, and number of bedrooms (*potential explanatory variables*).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Univariate Exploration

::::: columns
::: {.column width=65%}
```{r outwidth="100%",fig.asp=0.65}
grid.arrange(
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=price))+geom_histogram(binwidth=25,color="white")+theme_bw(base_size=11)+
    labs(x="Price (thousands of dollars)"),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=bedrooms))+geom_histogram(binwidth=1,color="white")+theme_bw(base_size=11)+
    labs(x="Number of Bedrooms")+scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:10),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_living))+geom_histogram(binwidth=100,color="white")+theme_bw(base_size=11)+
    labs(x="Total Square Footage"),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_above))+geom_histogram(binwidth=100,color="white")+theme_bw(base_size=11)+
    labs(x="Above-Ground Square Footage"),
  nrow=2)
```

:::

::: {.column width=35% .nonincremental}
<br><br>

- **Q**: How would you describe the distribution of `price`?

- **Q**: What do you expect the relationship between `price` and `bedrooms` to be like?
:::
:::::

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(2)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Bivariate Exploration, Multicollinearity

```{r outwidth="100%", fig.width=12, fig.height = 6}
grid.arrange(
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_living,y=price))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Sq. Footage",y="Price") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_above,y=price))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Ab.-Ground Sq. Ft.",y="Price") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=bedrooms,y=price))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Bedrooms",y="Price") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_living,y=sqft_above))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Sq. Footage",y="Ab.-Ground Sq. Ft.") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_living,y=bedrooms))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Sq. Footage",y="Bedrooms") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  ggplot(houses,aes(x=sqft_above,y=bedrooms))+geom_point(alpha=0.3)+theme_bw(base_size=10)+
    labs(x="Ab.-Ground Sq. Ft.",y="Bedrooms") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(size=16)),
  nrow=2, ncol = 3)
```


- **Q**: Which explanatory variables would be appropriate to include in our model? 

- **Q**: Do any pairs of explanatory variables suffer from multicollinearity?

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(3)
```

## Model Estimation

```{r}
mod <- lm(price ~ sqft_living + bedrooms, data = houses)
get_regression_table(mod)
```

::: nonincremental

- **Q**: What is the equation, including coefficient values, for the estimated model?

<!-- ::: fragment -->
<!-- $$ -->
<!-- \widehat{\text{price}} = 197 + 0.177*\text{sqrt_living} - 21.6*\text{bedrooms} -->
<!-- $$ -->
<!-- ::: -->

- **Q**: How should we interpret the **intercept** coefficient in our model?

<!-- - When `sqrt_living` and `bedrooms` are both 0, we expect/predict price to be $197,000 on average. -->

- **Q**: How should we interpret the coefficient for **Bedrooms**? Does this match your expectation?

<!-- - When the number of `bedrooms` increases by 1, we expect/predict price to **decrease** by $21,600 on average, **holding `sqft_living` constant**. -->

:::
     
```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(4)
```



------------------------------------------------------------------------

## LINE Assumptions

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5}
res <- get_regression_points(mod)
gg1 <- ggplot(res, aes(x = price_hat, y = residual)) +
  geom_point() + geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), lty = 2, color = "gray50")
gg2 <- ggplot(res, aes(x = residual)) + geom_histogram(color = "white")
gg3 <- ggplot(res, aes(sample = residual)) + geom_qq() + geom_qq_line()

gridExtra::grid.arrange(gg1, gg2, gg3, nrow = 2)

```

::: nonincremental

- **Q**: Does it seem like this model meets the four LINE assumptions? 

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(3)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Adjusted $R^2$

::: {style="font-size:0.85em;"}

What's the adjusted $R^2$ of our model?

```{r echo = TRUE}
get_regression_summaries(mod) %>% select("r_squared", "adj_r_squared")
```

::: fragment
Not super close to 1. Compare to a simpler model:
:::

::: fragment
```{r echo = TRUE}
small_mod <- lm(price ~ bedrooms, data = houses)
get_regression_summaries(small_mod) %>% select("r_squared", "adj_r_squared")
```
:::

::: fragment
Compare to a much bigger model with additional variables:

```{r echo = TRUE}
big_mod <- lm(price ~ bedrooms + bathrooms + sqft_living + sqft_above + sqft_lot + view + condition + yr_built,
              data = houses)
get_regression_summaries(big_mod) %>% select("r_squared", "adj_r_squared")
```
:::

- **Q**: Why are $R^2$ and adjusted $R^2$ different? 

:::

## Practice problem: Data Wrangling Pseudo-Code

<!-- Note to self: Solutions are in lab_review_session.qmd from last semester. -->

Looking at `pdxtrees` again:

::: {style="font-size:1.25em;"}

```{r echo=F, warning=F, message=F}
library(pdxTrees)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
near_Reed <- get_pdxTrees_parks(park = c("Woodstock Park", "Sellwood Riverfront Park", "Kenilworth Park"))
near_Reed <- near_Reed[near_Reed$Genus %in% c("Acer", "Quercus", "Pinus", "Thuja", "Pseudotsuga"), ] 
near_Reed <- near_Reed[, c("Genus", "DBH", "Condition", "Tree_Height", "Crown_Width_NS", "Park", "Native")]
near_Reed[c(1, 2, 46, 166, 322), ]
```

:::

<br><br>

**Write pseudo-code to**: Make a contingency table of whether trees in Woodstock Park are "big guys" or "little guys" (one variable) and whether they are native species or not (second variable). Trees are considered "big guys" when DBH > 30 or Tree_Height > 100 and "little guys" otherwise.

```{r echo=FALSE}
countdown::countdown(5)
```

## Practice problem: Data Wrangling Explaining Code

Now let's turn to the penguins data. 

::: {style="font-size:1.25em;"}

```{r, warning=F, message=F, echo=T, eval=F}
penguins %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex),
         island %in% c("Biscoe", "Dream")) %>%
  count(species, island, sex) %>%
  group_by(species, island) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  arrange(species, island, sex)
```
:::


<br><br>

**Explain what each line of code does in context, and sketch what the final data frame would look like.** Reminder that there are 3 different species in `penguins`: Adelies, Gentoos, and Chinstraps. It might be helpful to sketch what the data frame looks like at each intermediate step! 


```{r echo=FALSE}
countdown::countdown(7)
```

## Practice problem: More Linear Regression (skip?)

<!-- Note to self: Answers are in quiz folder from last semester. -->

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

In HW 4, we explored the results of the **Anchoring Effect Experiment** conducted during Lab 2. Our hypothesis is that the number a student saw on the paper slip (the `treatment`, either **82** or **531**) affected the student's guess for the number of dog breeds in the world (the response variable).

We can assess the relationship between the guessed number of dog breeds and the number received on the paper slip by running a regression. Below is a summary of this regression, where `treatment` is treated as a **categorical** explanatory variable.

:::

<br>

```{r echo = FALSE}
library(moderndive)
dogs <- read.csv("data/dogs_cleaned.csv")
dogs$treatment <- factor(dogs$treatment)
get_regression_table(lm(n_breeds ~ treatment, dogs))
```

<br>

- **Q1**: Write the equation for the **estimated regression line**.




- **Q2**: How should we interpret the "intercept" and "`treatment: High`" terms, given the context of the experiment?


```{r echo=FALSE}
countdown::countdown(3)
```

## Practice problem: More Linear Regression

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

In HW 4, we explored the results of the **Anchoring Effect Experiment** conducted during Lab 2. Our hypothesis is that the number a student saw on the paper slip (the `treatment`, either **82** or **531**) affected the student's guess for the number of dog breeds in the world (the response variable).

We can assess the relationship between the guessed number of dog breeds and the number received on the paper slip by running a regression. Below is a summary of this regression, where `treatment` is treated as a **categorical** explanatory variable.

:::

<br>

```{r echo = FALSE}
library(moderndive)
dogs <- read.csv("data/dogs_cleaned.csv")
dogs$treatment <- factor(dogs$treatment)
get_regression_table(lm(n_breeds ~ treatment, dogs))
```

<br>

- **Q3**: Suppose I had tested the effect of three different treatments: `82`, `531`, and `900`, instead of just `82` and `531`. What would be different about the regression model and the results table?


- **Q4**: Suppose `treatment` was actually a **quantitative** variable, with each student seeing a different number in $[0, 200]$. Suppose that then our regression model produced estimates $\widehat{\beta}_0 = 100$ and $\widehat{\beta}_1 = 4$. How should we interpret $\widehat{\beta}_0$ and $\widehat{\beta}_1$ now?

```{r echo=FALSE}
countdown::countdown(5)
```
